messages:
sophia: Quick sync — we need to align the long-term routing policy roadmap for multi-region + multi-tenant isolation. Primary asks: customer-driven residency, predictable evacuation behavior, and prioritization of launch work. I sketched three high-level bets and want input on prioritization and launch gates.

kevin: Can you spell out the SLO/budget constraints we need to hold? e.g. do we aim for 99.95% per-region availability or cross-region failover within X ms? Those numbers drive the design tradeoffs.

aj: From product/customer side: two enterprise asks to anchor on — FinBank needs hard data residency (no cross-region fallback unless explicitly allowed), and GamingCo wants automated cross-region failover with <200ms degradation for session continuity.

maria: Note on cost side — cross-region replication + duplicate KV caches will increase network egress and GPU warmup. We'll need a rough delta estimate before committing to a broad rollout. Suggest adding a perf spike to measure cache-warmup penalty.

ryan: Sales input: customers will want contractual language around evacuation windows and pinned-region guarantees. We need clear launch criteria so I can negotiate timelines (e.g., "regional pinning available for enterprise in Q3").

kevin: Suggest we boil policy primitives down to a small set of building blocks so we can mix-and-match per-tenant:
- hard_region_lock: no cross-region routing unless admin override
- soft_affinity: prefer local region, fallback to nearest compatible variant
- evacuate_slice: controlled tenant migration with eviction window and warmup

kevin: quick config example (proposal):
```
policy:
  name: soft-affinity
  affinity: regional
  fallback: nearest-compatible
  eviction_window: 30m
  canary_percent: 5
```

sophia: I like grounding on primitives. Proposed prioritization (phase plan):
- Phase 1 (Q3): hard_region_lock for contractual customers + migration tooling for manual evacuations (FinBank path)
- Phase 2 (Q4): soft_affinity + automated fallback policies, basic cost accounting, and SLA tests
- Phase 3 (H1 next year): evacuate_slice + fast failover steering, canary routing, full observability (per-tenant failover timelines)

sophia: Proposed launch gating checklist (short):
- infra spike demonstrates <X ms failover for canary workload
- SLO validation tests (latency p95, regional availability)
- Cost delta < Y% for sample workloads or opt-in pricing path
- Tenant migration API + dry-run tested
- Legal/contract language agreed for pinned-region customers

maria: For validation metrics, capture: regional p95 latency, cross-region failover time (cold vs warm), cache-warmup token cost, and egress delta per TB. Also flag runbook for partial evacuations.

aj: For migration UX, we should provide a tenant-level "dry-run" mode that simulates traffic steering and reports expected failover time and cost. Also require an automated rollback path.

sophia: Next steps: 1) technical spike to implement eviction_window semantics and measure warmup (owner: eng-runtime), 2) prodize migration API (owner: eng-platform), 3) define launch criteria document and runbook (owner: product + reliability). Can folks ack owners or suggest alternatives?

kevin: Ack for eng-runtime spike. I'll scope the kernel/cache changes and outline perf test matrix. :thumbsup:

maria: Ack for reliability; I'll own metrics/dashboarding and cost analysis.

ryan: I'll compile customer asks and draft a short contract clause for pinned-region commitments; will loop legal.

aj: I'll prepare migration UX spec and a dry-run flow.

deploy-bot: Reminder: infra spike window scheduled 2026-07-12 18:00 UTC — please add any required infra flags to the spike ticket.

sophia: Thanks everyone — I'll convert this thread into a concise launch-criteria doc and share a PR to the roadmap board by EOD tomorrow. If no objections, we'll lock Phase 1 priorities and start the runtime spike. :rocket:
